input: Good morning, everyone. I wanted to share a short reflection on a podcast episode I listened to last week, which followed a single school enrolment form through the course of one family's year. The episode was titled "The Blue Form," and it was produced by a local education trust in the north of the city. I found it moving, and also rather unsettling, in ways I did not expect. The host, Marguerite Osei, began with a simple premise. She had found a discarded enrolment form in the lobby of Hartwell Primary School, dated the fourteenth of March 2019, with most of its boxes left empty. The form belonged to a boy named Tomasz Varga, who had just moved to the area with his grandmother. Marguerite spent the next several episodes trying to understand why the form had never been completed. What struck me most was how much the form asked for, and how little it allowed for explanation. Every field expected a neat answer. Under "Parent or guardian," there was a single line. Under "Reason for leaving previous school," there was a set of tick boxes, none of which matched Tomasz's situation. I found myself sympathising with whoever had sat at that desk, pen in hand, unable to fit their life into the spaces provided. I should be honest that I did not agree with every conclusion the podcast reached. At times the episode leaned heavily on emotion, and I would have liked more attention to the administrative pressures faced by the school's office staff. Still, the central point was persuasive. Forms are never neutral. They quietly decide whose circumstances count as normal. I would therefore recommend the episode to anyone who works with families, whether in schools, councils or community groups. It is short, carefully made, and it may well change how you read the next form you are asked to sign. Thank you for listening.

My name is Carol Jennings, and my account number is 4471-082, though I think that's on the receipt I'll attach later. I'm calling about a washing machine I bought from your store on Route 9 in Millbrook back on March 14th. It's the Harmon Eco 700 front loader, and I paid for the extended warranty too, so I was hoping this would be an easy one.

Here's what's happened.

About three weeks after we got it, so that would be around April 5th, it started making this loud grinding noise during the spin cycle. At first I thought it was just a sock or a shoe stuck in the drum, so I opened it up and checked, and there was nothing in there. I ran it again on a normal cotton load and the noise got worse. By the following week it was shaking so hard it walked itself across the laundry room floor. My husband, Tom, had to put a brick under one of the feet just to keep it from hitting the dryer.

I called the support line on April 9th, and the representative, I think his name was Devon, was really nice. He walked me through a reset and said the drum bearings might need replacing. He opened a service ticket, number 88215, and said a technician would come out within five to seven business days. I wrote that down on the pad by the phone, so I have it.

The technician didn't come within that window.

Nobody came for eleven days. When I called back on April 22nd, I got a different person, and she told me the ticket had been "pending parts" but she couldn't say when the parts would arrive. She didn't seem to have any updates in the system, and she couldn't explain why nobody had called me. I asked to speak to a supervisor, and I was put on hold for about twenty-five minutes before the line just dropped.

So I'm writing to ask for a few things.

First, I'd like a technician scheduled for a specific date in the next week, with a confirmation email to me at carol.jennings@example.com. Second, since the machine has been out of commission for nearly a month now, I'd like a credit toward the laundromat costs we've had to pay, which come to about ninety dollars so far. I have the receipts and I'll send photos. Third, I'd really appreciate it if someone could tell me whether the extended warranty covers the bearing replacement, because the last person I spoke to wasn't sure.

I know these things happen, and I don't want to make anyone's day harder than it already is. Devon was lovely, and I think the people in the store were genuinely trying to help. I just need this fixed, and I'd like to hear back from someone who can actually see the whole history of the ticket.

You can reach me at 555-0147 most weekday afternoons, or by email.

Thank you for taking the time to listen to this.

I'm going to go ahead and send the receipts now.

Okay, that's it.

Bye now.
